As your run of bad luck has been going on for a while, you decide to take your chances. The realm is vast, its forests dark and the roads dangerous. But courier runs pay richly, so you dare to venture outside the protective walls of your city... This sounds like a flashback to the Middle Ages? Well, come in and find out... Collect gold coins, deal with gangs of robbers to outmaneuver your competition, and explore remote corners of the realm using runes. Every step you take needs to be well planned. Your opponents are hot on your heels! After all, who knows how many more potions there are? Whoever manages to collect 20 gold coins the fastest, wins the game. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 26 mn Complexity: 3 / 5 Play Treos and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Welcome to Treos! Head out and explore the world: complete quests and side quests to collect enough gold faster than the others. The first player to collect 20 gold wins the game. Contents 1 Sunrise: Planning 2 Morning, Midday, Evening: movement 2.1 Town 2.2 Fort 2.3 Inn 2.4 Secret Place 2.5 Portal 2.6 Highwaymen 3 Ways to Earn Gold 4 Sundown: clean-up Sunrise: Planning Each player draws 5 cards from their deck and assigns them face down: One on the bid space: the higher the card number on the bottom left of the card you place there, the earlier you will move during this round. Three on the 3 different day turns: considering the movement options on the cards they place there. The last card may be replaced on top of their card deck or discarded. Players also place an intrigue marker face down on each of the movement cards for the 3 daytimes (NB: in this BGA adaptation, you just have to choose a space for the "move highwayman token"). Morning, Midday, Evening: movement According to their turn order markers, each player takes one turn: reveal the movement card and the intrigue marker and then move accordingly the pawn and (if the "move highwayman token" has been revealed) one highwayman. Reaching new places: Town Complete a quest, take a new quest card (if you have a free space for it). Fort Get the fort's weapon, if you don't already have it (triggers character-specific power). Inn Get a side quest. If you are the first entrant to the inn, you get 1 gold. Secret Place Reveal the power of the secret place: get a movement card, get a side quest, or open a Portal. If you are the first entrant to the Secret Place, you get 1 gold. Portal Free move to another portal. Highwaymen Highwaymen block and prevent you from moving through or onto the space they are standing on. Move the highwayman using the same movement card with which you have just moved your character token. Again, you may use fewer moves than allowed or not move any highwayman at all. Highwaymen may not move onto or through towns and forts, or any space occupied by a character token. They may, however, move onto inns, secret places, and spaces without character tokens. Any number of highwaymen may share the same space. You must move your character marker before you move the highwayman. Ways to Earn Gold 1-3 Gold for completing a quest 0-4 Gold for collecting a new weapon 1 gold for discovering an inn 1 gold for discovering a secret place Carolijn only: 1 gold for completing a side quest Sundown: clean-up All players discard their cards into their respective discard pile. An Event is revealed, providing a special rule for the next turn. [Rating: 2/10] Plays like an asymmetric Chutes and Ladders deckbuilder. Not for me. The tedium of Talisman without the fun of the highjinks.

[Rating: 3/10] I'm not finding much of interest in this hope you get the cards you need to get where you want to go game. Feels like it may also go to the person who gets the most quests requiring minimal travel - tough luck if you keep getting quests that require you to move to a city further away than other players.

[Rating: 3/10] 3 = Bad, won't likely play this again -  This is for sure, since this game adds nothing to the hobby and has nothing interesting going on. It's the same from game to game and feels like a design from 2005 or so. We already have to many board game nowadays, I don't get why such a game is released by such a well known publisher. The German board game designs are not the state of the art anymore. For more exciting designs we have to look in Eastern Europe.

[Rating: 3/10] Tried it again and it's the most frustrating game in years. Digital.  It's like route building/navigation but they make it significantly harder but in an awkward way

I wouldn't mind that too much, if it weren't for the fact that this game also overstays its welcome by setting the target win condition to be getting 20 coins. [Rating: 5/10] As far as programming games go, TREOS was okay.  The cards themselves were fine, but I really didn’t like the map, a bit too busy and at times confusing to look at when planning your routes.  The questing itself felt superfluous because in both of my plays I got most of my points by collecting weapons and the random gold setup on inns and special locations.  Movement can often be quite frustrating because if you don’t have the right cards, even if your destination is one space away you may not be able to get to it.  A hard one to recommend unless you really like this style of gameplay.
